newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope says Sarajevo trip to show Church solidarity.
newsitem.headline: Pope says Sarajevo trip to show Church solidarity.

text.p: Pope John Paul said on Wednesday that his forthcoming trip to Sarajevo would show the Roman Catholic Church's solidarity with suffering people in the former Yugoslavia.
The Polish Pontiff is due to make a long-awaited visit to the Bosnian capital on Saturday and Sunday.
The Pope told a weekly general audience that Sarajevo was "a symbol of the tragedies to afflict Europe in the 20th century".

His 25-hour visit is to a land torn apart by four-years of inter-communal war underscored by religious divisions. "This apostolic visit is also a visit of peace which bears witnhess to the solidarity of the Church with suffering people," he said.

The Pontiff, who had to cancel a visit to Sarajevo in September 1994 because of security fears, is due to hand out peace prizes to four humanitarian organisations for work carried out during the Bosnian war when he visits Sarajevo.
The 76-year-old Pontiff will give $50,000 in cash rewards to groups representing the Roman Catholic, Serb-Orthodox, Moslem and Jewish faiths.
Fresh security fears have been raised over the Pope's historic trip after three rifle grenades were fired at a Roman Catholic monastery in central Bosnia last weekend.
